description: The National Bridge Inventory holds the structure inventory and appraisal data that US States, federal agencies and tribal governments submit to the Federal Highway Administration each year under the National Bridge Inspection Standards: location, route carried and crossed, structure type and material, year built and reconstructed, dimensions, traffic, load ratings, inspection dates and condition ratings of deck, superstructure, substructure and culvert, from which the Good, Fair and Poor condition measure is derived. Coverage is national for the United States and territories at the level of individual bridges; the 2025 release lists 624,193 highway bridges. Annual ASCII files for 1992 to 2025 are free downloads, as fixed-width or comma-delimited text in zip files per State or for the nation, with a record format guide; public highway bridge data is final by 15 June each year. Data from 2026 on follow the new Specifications for the National Bridge Inventory (SNBI), with a data crosswalk and transition tool for historic records. Caveats: 2025 was the last Coding Guide year, so series must be crosswalked, the structurally deficient label was replaced in 2018, load fields are in metric tons, and some territories did not report. The NBI is the standard asset inventory for bridge fragility, hazard exposure, network resilience, cascading failure and maintenance investment studies of US road networks, together with the HPMS road network catalogued here.
